method: Static reverse engineering with dnfile/dncil CIL disassembly, source call/data-flow review, PE parsing, independent managed-resource extraction, fontTools structure/glyph/program parsing, forager provenance fetches, cleave facts and before/after atomscan scans. No sample code executed.

samples.identification: Sentio Studio ieo Windows PDF reader preview 0.1.2 installer
samples.marker_line: ieo preview installer: consent-based reader; correct opcode/name traits
execution_trace: CLR entry token 0x06000007 -> IeoPreviewInstaller.Main at RVA 0x2b44. QA mode requires a GUID; ordinary installation asks for confirmation. Refuses install/update/uninstall while its own installed reader is open.

Reads Payload and Manifest managed resources, checks the product and SHA-256 of the ZIP, rejects duplicate/unlisted members and invalid relative paths, imposes entry and total size bounds, verifies each file hash/size, stages under LocalApplicationData/Programs/ieo-preview, and moves to a content-versioned release directory.

All 226 extracted files match the manifest, including reader executable, WebView2 libraries, bundled React/PDF.js assets, sample PDFs and codecs. Manifest consistency is self-integrity, not publisher authentication.

Creates Desktop/Start-menu shortcuts through WScript.Shell COM and registers per-user uninstall metadata. Updates a Run value only if an existing value belongs to this installation and has the expected hidden-launch form. Uninstall removes owned shortcuts/Run value/uninstall key while preserving reading data and rollback versions.

Reader StartupRegistration.Set explicitly enables/disables its own Run value when the settings UI requests it. Hidden mode waits in a tray; QA-only pipe supports testing operations. These are real dual-use capabilities, retained as notable findings.

GoogleAuth.Browser creates random state and PKCE verifier/challenge, binds a TcpListener only to loopback, opens accounts.google.com OAuth in the browser, checks callback state, exchanges the code at oauth2.googleapis.com/token, and obtains the current user through the Google Drive about endpoint. Its Vault uses CurrentUser DPAPI to store its own refresh authorization.

ReaderContext.Resource serves the virtual https://ieo.example origin from packaged dist assets and permits Google APIs. It validates paths and allowed methods; ieo.example is not an external C2 server. Frontend sync operates on user-selected PDFs and its own Drive app-data. Bundled migration.js copies and verifies the app-owned IndexedDB/profile data with a fresh writer identity.

No hidden shellcode or encrypted executable was found. High entropy comes from a conventional ZIP managed resource. The two RDTSCP matches are compressed-resource bytes, not native instructions executed by this IL-only assembly. Dynamic C# binder calls create shortcuts; they do not constitute reflective payload loading.

provenance.installer_signature: Unsigned; no Authenticode security directory. Version resource is sparse and carries 0.0.0.0. PE checksum is unset.
provenance.embedded_webview2: Microsoft-named signatures have matching Authenticode file digests. osslsigncode could not validate the signing/timestamp trust chains because the local issuer roots are absent; full platform trust is not asserted.

samples.verdict_basis: Consistent consent-based PDF reader behavior plus a byte-identical release on the referenced product website outweigh generic static detections. Nothing establishes abuse on a victim machine. The unsigned, new, high-entropy managed installer with Run-key and OAuth functionality plausibly attracted heuristic/ML collection. The actual original collection reason and deployment circumstances are unknown; benign judgement routes to sighted quarantine.
limitations: Static analysis; no runtime execution or end-to-end Google authentication.
The installer scan does not automatically expose all members of its managed ZIP resource; those files were carved, verified and scanned separately.
Public installed-app OAuth client configuration is present; this is not evidence of stolen credentials.

samples.identification: Official npm nx 21.6.8 monorepo build CLI tarball
samples.marker_line: Nx 21.6.8: upstream build CLI; preserve dual-use behavior
execution_trace: package.json postinstall -> bin/post-install.js. Runs the normal platform check only for the main workspace package, and verifies/updates the Nx Cloud client only when workspace configuration enables Nx Cloud. The hook times out after 30 seconds and logs errors without making install fatal.

Nx Cloud update manager requests /nx-cloud/client/verify from NX_CLOUD_API, configured enterprise URL, or cloud.nx.app; downloads/extracts a client bundle and requires its entry point. This is actual network-to-module activation in a configured cloud build tool, retained without claiming unauthorized execution.

Native module loading selects declared @nx platform packages or its shipped WASI fallback. It copies native modules into a workspace-scoped cache to avoid file locks, loads them, and restores Module._load. Task execution, Git operations, package installation, filesystem traversal, environment reads, daemon IPC and cloud cache operations serve the build CLI.

AI configuration is an explicit CLI operation that configures supported agents/MCP integrations and can load a provenance-checked recent Nx package. The install hook does not launch AI agents to search secrets. The package contains no S1ngularity telemetry.js, token-hunting hook, public-repository leak routine, or shutdown shell-profile modification.

Fetched all 35 currently resolved direct dependencies and all 10 pinned native optional dependencies using forager, retaining .forage.json provenance. Static scans of the 45 archives found no hostile/suspicious rules. The reviewed node-machine-id implementation invokes platform identity commands and hashes the result for cache identity; this is real dual-use behavior.

Fetched current cloud verification response and its referenced client bundle. Its exports, API calls, worker entry points and run/cache/distributed-agent paths implement Nx Cloud. Its 6.9MB index uses opaque _0x variable names and XOR arithmetic; this real obfuscation remains suspicious. The matcher does not establish a decoder or evaluator, so its description and home were corrected.
samples.verdict_basis: The exact published tarball implements the expected build tool and its installation paths contain no malicious replacement. Nx documents S1ngularity-compromised versions including 21.6.0, not 21.6.8; code and hash comparison, not version alone, support this judgement. A source could have overgeneralized the earlier Nx compromise. Its actual collection reason and deployment context are unknown.
limitations: There is no installation lockfile. Semver dependencies were resolved at analysis time; current cloud responses and dependencies cannot prove the contents of a historical installation.
Transitive dependency trees and every possible enterprise URL/configuration were not exhaustively analyzed.
The source analyzer reports bounded-flow limitations in some large/complex files; source inspection supplements those gaps.

samples.marker_line: Cousine 1.00: valid font subset with normal glyphs and hinting
execution_trace: Validated the SFNT directory and all table checksums, parsed all 216 glyphs and their coordinates/composite references, cmap, font program and prep program. All 17 tables are in bounds and the final table ends exactly at byte 43912; there is no appended payload.

The file exposes 212 mapped Unicode characters. Glyph hint programs and the 1797-byte fpgm and 1130-byte prep programs decode as normal TrueType hint instructions. maxp declares 90 functions, no instruction definitions and composite depth 1. No malformed table structure or exploit-oriented program was found.

DSIG is an 8-byte empty signature table with zero signature records; the file is not authenticated as digitally signed. The firing signature-recognized trait describes the container magic, not a verified cryptographic signature.

Fetched current upstream Google Fonts Cousine for comparison: it is version 1.241 with more glyphs, not a byte-identical original. All 212 mapped characters exist upstream and 82 have exactly matching outlines. Attribution/license links resolve to the SIL Open Font License and Monotype; they are font metadata, not network calls.
samples.verdict_basis: A structurally valid font with ordinary outlines and hinting supports benign rendering data. It contains no supported malicious capability. It may have been collected as an asset inside a hostile bundle; no original container or deployment evidence establishes why it was labeled malware.
samples.trait_changes: None; both font format observations remain accurate.

changes.reason: Hex bytes in a text section do not establish executed RDTSCP. Preserved identical matcher, count, section, architecture, size, exclusion and notable severity; updated the catalog-loader consumer.

Filename reference establishes neither temporary location nor process creation. Preserved matcher/scope/notable severity and exact download-manager consumer; removed unsupported execution ATT&CK attribution. Audited process/create ancestors: real launch claims should no longer be satisfied solely by a filename.

Required evidence is opaque variable declarations plus repeated XOR expressions, not decoding or evaluation. Preserved suspicious severity, required atoms, platform/type scope and staged-cleanup consumer.

Removed an objective-tier duplicate of a neutral Drive API reference. It supplied no source-to-send chain or unauthorized result. Canonical notable API detection remains; no hostile or suspicious cloud-transfer rule was removed. The two neutral runner co-occurrence consumers now explicitly include the canonical API observation instead of depending on the misplaced alias.

regression_controls: Focused behavior-backed downloader, opcode and other controls remain; inert catalog strings no longer preserve the unsupported hostile loader claim.
shared_rule_audit: Inspected exact and ancestor consumers and positive fixtures. The analysis-catalog fixture has two TLS callbacks that execute RDTSCP but never compare or branch on the results; probe strings are unreferenced, and the overlay is repeated filler. The combined-service-loader PE fixtures contain only serialized API names and diagnostics behind a ret stub. Their prior hostile expectations have been removed; atomic marker and opcode observations remain.
classifier: All three original samples are BENIGN before and after. The installer raw aggregate probability rises after taxonomy correction, but all model classes remain 0. Nx and font local scans are unchanged. The fetched client remains suspicious for real obfuscation. Model v18.18 warns that its feature specification predates extractor v19; model output is treated as a lead.
coverage: The unsupported hostile anti-analysis catalog composite was removed; its label and opcode observations remain at accurate severities. The two serialized-loader composites and their remote-thread consumer were removed because marker co-occurrence and serialized API names do not establish reachable payload or injection code. Atomic API and diagnostic references remain. Behavior-backed hostile detections elsewhere are unchanged.
